title: Snowflake Bets on Corporate Data Gateway, Embedding OpenAI and Anthropic Models
summary: Snowflake integrates OpenAI and Anthropic models into its corporate data gateway
detailed: Snowflake integrated OpenAI and Anthropic models within its platform perimeter, positioning itself as an enterprise data gateway and agent manager rather than building base LLMs.
The company launched the Cortex AI Gateway to apply human employee data access permissions, enforce cost limits, and block prompt injection attacks for AI agents.
Snowflake introduced Business Ontology as a public test service to unify department-specific definitions and resolve conflicting AI answers.
New task execution bots, CoCo and CoWork, are currently in private preview and already see active usage across thousands of developer and employee accounts.
The product strategy emphasizes corporate data governance and human-in-the-loop approval over fully autonomous core data system modifications.
sentences: Snowflake has staked its bet in the enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) agent market on data control rather than model performance.

Instead of building its own large language models (LLMs), the company plans to borrow OpenAI's and Anthropic's models within its own security perimeter and position itself as the platform that connects corporate internal data and business context while managing execution permissions.
The company unveiled AI agent management features and new bots to coincide with Expedition 2026, its own three-day online event that began on the 3rd (local time).
The blueprint calls for handling everything on its platform — from the information AI needs to understand a company's circumstances, to actually carrying out tasks, to post-hoc controls.
"Corporate data is the key if AI is to work properly in an enterprise environment," Christian Kleinerman, Snowflake's senior vice president of product, said at a pre-event media briefing.

"You absolutely need business context to guarantee results." The logic is that no matter how capable a model is, it cannot handle work accurately without knowing the company's revenue definitions or data access permissions.
Snowflake is a data cloud company founded in the United States in 2012 that helps enterprises gather data scattered across their organizations into one place for analysis and use.
As of September 2026, it has more than 14,500 customers worldwide.
If OpenAI, with ChatGPT, and Anthropic, with Claude, are companies building the "brains," Snowflake is positioning itself as the gateway that manages the data and rules those brains work with.
The Cortex AI Gateway unveiled at the event is a checkpoint that every AI agent in a company must pass through.
It applies the same data access permissions used for human employees to agents, and sets limits by tallying costs per agent, per team and per user.
It blocks executions that fall outside permissions and also prevents prompt injection attacks that trick AI into issuing unintended commands.
It also includes a feature that reduces wasted spending by selecting expensive, high-performance models or cheaper ones depending on task difficulty.
The Business Ontology, which resolves confusion caused by different departments interpreting terms differently, is being offered as a public test service.

It is a mechanism for unifying, through a company-wide definition approved by the relevant managers, the problem of AI giving conflicting answers to the same question because HR and finance define "employee turnover" by different standards.
Rather than requiring companies to build new "semantic views" — the existing per-department data interpretation framework — it adds company-wide shared terms and relationships on top.
Actual task execution is handled by CoCo, an agent for developers, and CoWork, for general employees.
The bots unveiled at the event plan their own work once a user sets a goal, and continue tasks even while the user is away.
Preparing customer meeting materials or checking data processing status are typical examples.
They are designed to call on the user when an important judgment or approval is needed.
The new bots are in private preview with select customers, while the existing CoCo and CoWork are used in more than 9,100 and 5,800 accounts, respectively.
In the data management area, AI finds errors and proposes fixes, but humans decide whether to apply them to actual production systems.

Kleinerman said having AI change core data systems without human intervention is not desirable at this stage, and explained that even if repetitive work is reduced, approval of change plans and verification of results must remain.
He advised enterprises to start by applying the technology to narrowly scoped, specific tasks rather than pursuing company-wide deployment from the outset, then expand after operational experience.
The competitive landscape is complicated.

OpenAI in February launched Frontier, an enterprise platform for building and managing agents, and began providing business context by connecting data warehouses and customer relationship management (CRM) systems.
Anthropic in April introduced Claude Managed Agents, an operations platform with security and governance features.
The business areas of model companies and data companies have begun to overlap on business context and control.
Snowflake cites its more than a decade of investment in data and data governance as its differentiator.
It also predicted that rather than a single model company dominating the market, companies that tie multiple models and data into business workflows will gain competitiveness.
Kleinerman stressed that it is easier to bring AI models to where the data is than to build a new trusted environment from scratch centered on corporate data.
Note: Both sides are expanding business context and governance features, and their territories are overlapping.
Snowflake expects agent adoption in the South Korean market to take off first in the financial industry.

Bala Kasiviswanathan, Snowflake's vice president of AI and developer experience, said South Korean banks, insurers and securities firms are already building agents for tasks such as detecting anomalous transactions, customer support and managing insurance claims.

Because financial firms face strict regulatory and audit requirements, a system for tracking what an agent did with which data is essential, and he explained that Snowflake's approach of verifying access permissions and data provenance before execution can play to its strengths.
He named manufacturing, distribution and e-commerce as the next candidates for adoption after finance.
The move aligns with a shift in the weight of enterprise AI spending from the models themselves to data connectivity and control.
For enterprises, the deciding factor in adoption success is increasingly not which model they use but how safely they connect internal data to AI and how they manage costs and permissions.
Still, with OpenAI and Anthropic expanding into the same territory, the contest for leadership between data platforms and model companies is expected to continue for the time being.
